title: Fixed Long Blunt Plate and Upright Eye Grip Froe
description: One newly authored whole fixed froe-inspired woodworking display. A single connected metal head extends from one thick annular end eye into a long broad constant-thickness blunt plate, with no separate poll or bulbous axe wedge. The head has a genuine full vertical through-eye in isolation, occupied by one complete gently shaped upright wooden handle in the fixed assembly. The long plate and single perpendicular end grip form the characteristic L silhouette; unlike the old drawknife there are no two returned tangs and parallel double grips, and unlike the display axe the socket sits at the end of a long flat plate rather than within a short thick curved-bit head. The broad head underside is only a static display datum. Two closed editable meshes and three opaque constant face-material roles; one prop zero scenes. All vertex geometry new, no old head or handle imported. No sharpened edge, cutting/splitting action, impact, wood processing, joint strength, hand fit, manufacture, operation or safety capability. The assembled eye is not claimed empty. Rigging animation interaction not made.
